title: Hosted API SLA-to-Behavior Mapping PRD and Cutover Checklist
creator: Asha Kapoor
description:
Summary:
This PRD defines how Redwood maps product-level SLAs and service profiles to concrete endpoint behavior, acceptance criteria, and a staged cutover checklist for hosted API endpoints (chat, completions, embeddings, rerank). The primary goal is to ensure predictable performance and quality for customers while enabling safe rollout of behavioral and runtime changes.

Problem statement:
As we expand the hosted surface and introduce adaptive lanes, graded fallbacks, and model variants, product SLAs (latency, availability, cost targets, and quality bands) must translate into executable runtime behavior and operational guardrails. Past launches showed mismatches between SLA language and runtime routing (e.g., different fallbacks under capacity pressure), unclear quality regression gates, and incomplete telemetry coverage for acceptance. This ticket captures product requirements, acceptance tests, and a launch cutover checklist to avoid those gaps.

Goals / success metrics (quantitative where possible):
- Latency: P95 token generation latency for the default fast lane <= 120 ms for 16-token slices on c5-standard profiles; end-to-end request P95 (including network) <= 250 ms for small completions (<= 64 tokens) in us-west region.
- Availability: 99.9% regional availability for hosted endpoints over a 30-day window for paid customers.
- Quality: No more than 2% degradation in eval pass-rate (weighted intent & safety tests) compared to baseline model per endpoint type after model swaps.
- Cost: No more than 12% increase in per-token cost for production traffic when enabling prefix KV cache + batching suggestions compared to current production baseline.
- Operational: 100% trace coverage (request id -> model variant -> kernel path) for production samples during the canary slice.

Scope (in-scope):
- Define per-endpoint SLA mapping (chat/completions/embeddings/rerank) to runtime behaviors: lane selection, fallback hierarchy, caching policies, and batching targets.
- Define acceptance criteria and automated checks (e2e smoke, perf, and eval suites).
- Create the staged cutover checklist (canary slices, telemetry validation, rollback criteria, gradual ramp).
- Document rollout knobs exposed to Console and API (feature flags, tenant-level lane overrides, deterministic seeding).

Out of scope:
- Low-level kernel optimizations (ENG will own implementation tasks).
- Dedicated/private deployment rollout specifics (this PRD focuses on hosted API; Dedicated will mirror policies in a follow-up).

Functional requirements:
1) SLA profile definitions: product must expose named profiles (eg. fast, balanced, cost-optimized) with explicit targets for latency, availability, and quality banding for each endpoint type. Profiles should map into runtime config documents that ENG accepts.
2) Fallback hierarchy: for each profile define ordered fallback list (exact model variant -> smaller context model -> compatible quantized variant -> degraded fast-mode producing shorter responses) and explicit behavior for streaming vs non-streaming requests.
3) Prefix/KV caching policy: host-level default cache TTLs and tenant opt-out; caching must be transparent to behavioral tests and must not introduce stale outputs for stateful chat sessions (session-bound caching validations required).
4) Batching latencies: target batch sizing logic must include soft-latency caps and hard SLO enforcement; product-level config will define acceptable latency uplift thresholds for batch-induced cost reductions.
5) Eval-driven quality gates: integrate a deterministic evaluation harness (seeded prompts + safety probes) that runs on canary traffic with defined pass thresholds to allow promotion.
6) Observability: emit enriched telemetry for every request including profile, chosen fallback, cache hit/miss, batching windows, kernel selection, and eval tag when applicable.

Non-functional requirements:
- Security/compliance: ensure KMS-backed model keys are not leaked in logs; audit events are emitted for profile changes.
- Scalability: runtime changes must not reduce regional capacity below current SLAs during rollout; autoscaler policies must be honored.
- Testability: every accepted change requires automated smoke (integration), perf (synthetic traffic at representative QPS), and eval runs (quality regression).

Acceptance criteria (must all be met to mark Done):
1) Documentation: Product page describing SLA profiles and mapping to runtime config published in internal Console docs and Drive (link provided in docs_links).
2) Perf gates: Synthetic perf test run against canary slice shows P95 token latency within 10% of target for 3 consecutive runs and no single-run regression > 20%.
3) Quality gates: Eval harness against canary traffic shows weighted pass-rate >= baseline - 2% and no critical safety fail. All failing prompts must be triaged and actioned before ramp.
4) Telemetry: Traces and logs include profile, fallback reason, cache hit, batch size, kernel tag, and model variant for 100% of canary requests.
5) Rollout automation: Console feature-flag + API support to toggle profile per-tenant and to set canary slice percentage (0.1%, 1%, 5%, 25%, 100%).
6) Rollback criteria defined and tested: automated rollback triggers on (a) availability drop > 0.2% absolute vs baseline during slice, (b) P95 latency > 30% above target for two consecutive intervals, or (c) quality gate failure per eval harness.
7) Security sign-off: Security review completed with remediation of any telemetry leaks; KMS integration validated.

Rollout & launch checklist (owner initials in parentheses):
- Pre-cutover (PM/ENG/Security)
  - Publish SLA profile docs and runtime mapping (PM - Asha).
  - Create canary evaluation set for each endpoint (PM + Research - Liam).
  - Ensure ENG feature flag hooks exist for profile and tenant override (ENG - S. Martinez).
  - Confirm telemetry schema with Observability (ENG/Observability - R. Patel).
  - Security review & KMS validation complete (Security - J. Morales).

- Canary slice execution (owners):
  - Deploy runtime config to canary pool (ENG - deployment owner).
  - Run perf/soak tests at representative QPS for 3 x 30-minute windows (SRE - K. Nguyen).
  - Run eval harness on canary traffic and produce report (Research/PM - Liam/Asha).
  - Validate 100% trace coverage and dashboards show expected signals (Observability - R. Patel).
  - Stakeholder review meeting after first passing run, decide ramp (PM/Eng/SRE).

- Ramp plan (staged percentages): 0.1% -> 1% -> 5% -> 25% -> 100% with at least 24-hour guardrails between steps and passing perf+eval checks at each step.

- Post-cutover (first 7 days):
  - Daily quality regression report and operational health digest (PM/Eng/SRE).
  - Cost delta analysis vs baseline (Finance/PM).
  - Capture learnings and update runbook (PM).

Dependencies & risks:
- ENG work to surface runtime flags and telemetry (ENG-8421). If delayed, cannot run gated canary.
- Eval coverage maturity: If the eval harness lacks coverage for a high-frequency failure mode, regressions may be missed. Risk mitigation: expand probe corpus pre-cutover.
- Autoscaler interactions: aggressive batching optimizations might cause autoscaler thrashing under synthetic load. Mitigation: conservative batching thresholds during ramp.
- Customer-visible behavior: changing fallback ordering could alter outputs for a minority of users; include migration notes and tenant-level opt-outs.

Open questions (must be resolved before canary):
1) Should deterministic seeding be on by default for the fast profile or opt-in per-tenant? (Options: default-on, default-off, tenant opt-in).
2) What is the authoritative metric for per-tenant availability (region-aggregated vs global)?
3) For streaming requests, how do we quantify and enforce partial-response latency SLOs?

Stakeholders (names and roles):
- Product: Asha Kapoor (owner), Priya Rao (support lead)
- Engineering: Liam Chen (runtime PM), Sofia Martinez (serving lead)
- SRE/Observability: Kevin Nguyen, Rishi Patel
- Security & Compliance: Jorge Morales
- Research/Quality: Mei Lin (eval lead)
- Finance: Daniel Ortega (cost analysis)
acceptance_criteria: 1) Docs published in Drive + Console help. 2) Perf gates: P95 within 10% of target across 3 runs. 3) Eval gates: weighted pass-rate >= baseline - 2% with no critical safety failures. 4) 100% trace coverage of canary traffic. 5) Feature-flag and per-tenant override exist. 6) Rollback triggers defined and tested. 7) Security sign-off obtained.
rollout_checklist: Pre-cutover: docs, canary eval set, feature-flag hooks, telemetry schema, security review. Canary: deploy config, perf/soak tests, eval run, trace validation, stakeholder review. Ramp: 0.1%->1%->5%->25%->100% with 24h gates. Post-cutover: daily reports, cost delta, runbook updates.
notes: This PRD intentionally focuses on the product->runtime contract and minimally on implementation details. ENG ticket ENG-8421 contains the low-level work and readiness checklist. Coordinate with Dedicated product owners to ensure parity after hosted rollout.
